rows.why: The examples include 2d = 172800000 and 1d0h0m0s0ms, so they depend on which units exist and whether a day unit is one of them. The pick supports d, h, m, s and ms. Item 8 (zero values) is close too, since 0s and the zero components must be accepted, and its pick does accept them.
Item 6 asks how surrounding whitespace is handled. The pick trims leading and trailing whitespace, so '  45m\n' parses to 2700000.

This scenario mixes several rejection questions. Item 5 covers the most rows: 1.5h, -3s, +3s and the full-width digit '３s'. The pick rejects any component that does not start with ASCII digits, so all four fail. Other rows belong to other items (90→1, 3S→3, '1h 30m' and '3 s'→6, empty→7, 3w→2). Note that the row 05s must be rejected, but item 8's pick accepts leading zeros, so the implementation would still fail S3 on that row.
No item asks whether a count may exceed the next unit, as 90m does. Item 4 is about the order of units and repeated units, not the size of a count.
Item 4 asks about largest-to-smallest order and repeated units. The pick rejects both, which covers 30m1h, 1h1h, 1s500ms2s and 5ms1s.
Item 9 asks for the upper limit. The pick caps the total at 2^53-1 ms, which is 9007199254740991, and that value is allowed, so the largest duration parses.
Item 9 also asks what happens on overflow. The pick checks each component and the running sum and returns 0 with an error beyond 2^53-1, so both rows are rejected.

Item 10 asks which units formatting uses and whether zero components are shown. The pick breaks the value greedily into d/h/m/s/ms and omits zeros, giving 1m30s, 1h30m, 1d and 1d1h1m1s1ms. The 0→'0ms' row matches item 11, which also agrees.
The exact output string comes from the greedy d/h/m/s/ms breakdown with zeros omitted. 9007199254740991 breaks into 104249991d 8h 59m 0s 991ms, and dropping the 0s gives '104249991d8h59m991ms'.
No item asks whether formatted output parses back to the same number.

Item 12 asks what formatting does with negative or over-range values. The pick returns "" and an error below 0 or above 2^53-1, which covers -1, 2^53, MinInt64 and MaxInt64. The pick doesn't give the error text, so it doesn't settle whether the message contains 'milliseconds'.
